text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 17px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #23313d

g.text: A common-emitter stage inverts small signals around a separately established DC bias

text.style: font-size: 9px; font-family: 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #59636c

g.text: Grounded emitter, assumed I_CQ=1 mA,β=100,T=300 K,r_o=100 kΩ. Bias source establishes the operating point; coupling capacitors are AC shorts only in the midband
model. Bias network loading is omitted from the shown signal model, and v_in denotes actual base-emitter incremental voltage. A_v=−g_m(R_C||R_L||r_o)≈-63.41;10 mV
input gives≈0.634 V output amplitude. Small signal and output headroom are assumed.
